title: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.29052v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A typed decision maps evidence, a question and a fixed set of options to a probability for every option, computed in one forward pass, by reading a language model's logits or a small head over its hidden states, instead of generating and parsing text. The commercial system Jev popularised this System~1 interface, and open reproductions have followed. We report two uses of the pattern. \emph{Part I} describes an in-house System~1 judge that triages about 148K agentic coding session records for a training corpus. It replaces a frontier LLM judge that cost on the order of \$1,000 per pass and whose stored labels matched a fresh two-judge consensus on only 26.9\% of the sessions where the two judges agreed; a self-hosted frozen backbone with a rank-16 LoRA adapter and a pointer head answers three typed questions in one forward pass, judges 1,000 sessions in about three minutes of one GPU, about \$0.06 at a reference rate and roughly 1\% of t

translated_title: 我们自己的Jev：单次前向传播中的类型化决策，从自研裁判到开放LoRA模型
translated_abstract: 类型化决策将证据、问题和一个固定的选项集映射为每个选项的概率，只需一次前向传播即可完成，方式是读取语言模型的logits或在其隐藏状态上附加一个小型头部，而不是生成并解析文本。商业系统Jev推广了这种System 1接口，开源复现也随之出现。我们报告了该模式的两种用途。第一部分描述了一个自研的System 1裁判，它为一个训练语料库筛选了约14.8万条智能体编码会话记录。它取代了一个前沿LLM裁判——后者每轮处理的成本约在1,000美元量级，且在两位裁判达成一致的会话中，其存储的标签与新做的双裁判共识仅有26.9%吻合；一个自托管的冻结骨干网络，配合秩为16的LoRA适配器和指针头，可在一次前向传播中回答三个类型化问题，在一块GPU上约三分钟内即可判定1,000个会话，按参考价格计算成本约0.06美元，大约仅为前沿模型成本的1%……
tldr: 该论文提出用单次前向传播的“类型化决策”接口（直接读取logits或轻量指针头）替代生成式LLM裁判，其自研System 1裁判仅用一块GPU约3分钟、约0.06美元即可判定1,000个智能体编码会话，以约1%的成本取代每轮约1,000美元且标签一致性仅26.9%的前沿LLM裁判。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces typed decisions—mapping evidence, questions, and options to probabilities in a single forward pass via logits or a lightweight pointer head—and shows an in-house System 1 judge that triages 1,000 agentic coding sessions in about three minutes on one GPU for roughly $0.06, replacing a frontier LLM judge that cost ~$1,000 per pass with only 26.9% label agreement.
